EXPLORING THE EFFECT OF TEMPERATURE
ON ENZYME ACTIVITY IN PLANT CELLS

· Alex G. · Monica V. · Tessa H. · Aiko S. · Bill T.

INTRODUCTION

Enzymes are essential biological catalysts that regulate chemical reactions within cells. This study investigates how temperature influences enzyme activity in plant cells, specifically focusing on amylase, an enzyme that catalyzes the breakdown of starch. Understanding the relationship between temperature and enzyme activity can help optimize agricultural practices, such as enhancing crop resistance to temperature fluctuations and improving the efficiency of industrial processes that involve plant-based enzymes.

METHODOLOGY

SAMPLE PREPARATION

Corn leaf cells were isolated and homogenized to extract amylase enzymes. The enzyme activity was measured by the rate of starch breakdown.

TEMPERATURE VARIATION

Enzyme activity was tested at 0°C, 20°C, 40°C, 60°C, and 80°C. Reactions were incubated for 30 minutes at each temperature.

SUBSTRATE ADDITION

Starch solution was added to each reaction, providing a substrate for the amylase enzyme.

REACTION TERMINATION

The reactions were stopped after 30 minutes using an enzyme inhibitor, and glucose production was measured.

DATA ANALYSIS

Absorbance of glucose was measured using a spectrophotometer. Data were analyzed using ANOVA to assess statistical significance of temperature on enzyme activity.

RESULTS

OPTIMAL TEMPERATURE

Enzyme activity peaked at 40°C, where the amylase was most effective in catalyzing starch breakdown. At this temperature, the rate of glucose production was 50% higher than at lower or higher temperatures.

TEMPERATURE EFFECT
  • At 0°C, enzyme activity was minimal, with only 10% of the maximum activity observed at 40°C
  • At 20°C, enzyme activity was moderate, with a 30% increase in glucose production compared to 0°C
  • At 60°C, enzyme activity dropped significantly, with only 25% of the activity seen at 40°C
  • At 80°C, enzyme activity was nearly zero, indicating enzyme denaturation

DISCUSSION

The results suggest that temperature has a profound impact on enzyme activity, with amylase being most efficient at 40°C. The significant decline in activity at temperatures above 60°C supports the hypothesis that extreme heat denatures enzymes. This has implications for both agricultural biotechnology, where temperature resilience could be engineered, and for industrial enzyme applications, where optimal reaction conditions are critical for efficiency.

CONCLUSION

Amylase activity in plant cells is highly temperature-dependent, with an optimal temperature of 40°C for maximum efficiency. Understanding the temperature sensitivity of enzymes can help improve crop productivity under varying environmental conditions and optimize industrial enzyme processes.

ACKNOWLEDGMENTS

This study was funded by the Agricultural Science Research Fund. Special thanks to the Plant Biology Department at Greenfield University for providing the samples.

REFERENCES

  • Green, J. H., & Thomas, L. M. (2021). Temperature-dependent enzyme activity in plant cells: A comparative study. Journal of Plant Physiology, 98(2), 115–130. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jplphys.2021.0207
  • Zhang, Q., & Chen, Y. F. (2020). Effects of temperature fluctuations on enzyme kinetics in plant systems. Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications, 53(9), 245–259. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbrc.2020.0806
  • Patel, S. K., & Rivera, J. A. (2022). The impact of thermal stress on plant enzyme activity: Insights from cellular experiments. Plant Biochemistry Journal, 62(4), 410–425. https://doi.org/10.1098/pbj.2022.0404
